tagline: Out of a candidate's namesake town, past a groundwater lake.
intro: Just south of Lockwood, Interlake Road leaves Jolon Road and runs for the San Luis Obispo County line. The country at the start is a broad valley encompassed by the coastal mountains, given over to farms, cattle ranches and vineyards. The town's name honors Belva Lockwood, who ran for president in 1884 and 1888.
On the way the road passes Lake San Antonio. Past the county line it carries on, under a second scenic designation, toward Bee Rock and Lake Nacimiento.

moments.title: Lockwood
moments.text: The post office opened in 1888, the year Belva Lockwood made her second run for president on the Equal Rights Party ticket.

moments.title: Lake San Antonio
moments.text: Behind a 202-foot dam on the San Antonio River, the lake's main work is underground: its water seeps into the ground, and without it the river would be nearly dry in summer.
